To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the intensity of the oxygen-minimum zone off the coast of central Chile (36° S) intensified during the first half of the 20th century, 2) this intensification was associated with an increase in the abundance of anaerobic bacteria and micro-aerophillic eukaryotes, 3) the intensification was likely related to a decrease in upwelling intensity and/or a shift in upwelling location.

the intensity of the oxygen-minimum zone (OMZ) off Concepcion, Chile, has increased over the last century and that this increase in OMZ intensity was accompanied by a shift in the microbial community.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

interdecadal changes in oxygenation in bottom waters and in surface sediments off Concepción, in the eastern boundary of the subtropical South Pacific, are tightly coupled with changes in primary production.
the O2 minimum zone (OMZ) off Concepcion, Chile (~ 360 S) has been intensifying since at least the 1920s.
the interdecadal changes in O2 concentrations in bottom waters of the oxygen minimum off Concepcion were accompanied by a significant increase in the abundance and diversity of anaerobic microbes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxygenation changes in this area are likely to be related with the Pacific Decadal Variability.
oxygen depletion is not a recent phenomenon in the upwelled waters off Chile.
oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) can be highly dynamic over time, and that these changes can be reflected in sedimentary records.
